focus: P7 human gates over live belief context, decision-time re-evaluation, invalidation, reopen, timeout, and consequence-edge authorization boundaries
noveltyJustification: Repo 1 defined a durable fenced gate and Graphene supplied cold belief context plus consequence/timeout behavior; this pass adds the missing snapshot-versus-live distinction, canonical belief/evidence/topology/head anchors, semantic invalidation and versioned reopen, timeout fencing, and the boundary between human edge intent and downstream effect authorization.
keyFindings: BeliefContextSnapshotV1 materializes the exact question, options, consequence map, load-bearing belief truth/staleness/support, and evidence shown at gate opening
Belief domain truth and gate-context snapshot freshness are distinct projection facts
Gate context binds belief, evidence, topology, consequence, domain-head, audit-head, reducer-contract, authority-epoch, policy, version, and fence anchors
A decision is snapshot-bound intent that must re-evaluate all load-bearing anchors inside the authoritative decision boundary
Semantic drift appends gate invalidation and recovery reopens a new version/fence/context epoch rather than mutating the old ask
A human choice authorizes at most an edge-selection intent; downstream mutations and effects require current separate authorization
Timeout is an explicit current-context fenced transition and never a synthetic human approval
Graphene human goldens prove local deterministic consequences and timeout, not stale-context or decision-fencing safety

ruledOut.approach: Store only belief IDs or rendered prose as gate context
ruledOut.reason: It cannot prove the exact truth, support, staleness, evidence, and topology shown

ruledOut.approach: Treat the opening context snapshot as durable authority
ruledOut.reason: All load-bearing anchors may change before decision delivery

ruledOut.approach: Mutate a pending gate in place after context drift
ruledOut.reason: It destroys the audit distinction between old and replacement questions
Only named semantic dependencies should invalidate; unrelated churn is an availability risk

ruledOut.approach: Let approval directly execute a consequence or effect
ruledOut.reason: Human intent does not prove current claim, resource fence, budget, policy, or idempotency state

ruledOut.approach: Treat timeout as approval or a daemon-local write
ruledOut.reason: Silence has no human principal and a stale timer can race reopen or takeover

nextFocus: P7 durable fenced decision command and effect authorization composition
